subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Producing several different rough ideas before choosing one is part of which stage of the design process?
questions.explain: Generating ideas involves creating a range of possible solutions, often through sketching, before developing the best one.

questions.q: In an isometric drawing, vertical lines stay vertical and the other edges are drawn at:
questions.explain: Isometric drawings keep verticals upright and draw receding edges at 30 degrees to the horizontal to give a 3D impression.

questions.q: Primary research in the design process means gathering:
options: New, first-hand data such as your own surveys or interviews
Information from existing books, websites and reports
Data that is always out of date
questions.explain: Primary research is original, first-hand data collected directly, such as questionnaires, interviews or measurements.

questions.q: Secondary research in designing means using information that:
options: Already exists, such as books, websites and reports
You collect first-hand through your own survey
questions.explain: Secondary research uses existing, second-hand sources such as books, articles and websites gathered by others.

questions.q: Developing a chosen idea differs from generating ideas because developing involves:
options: Refining and improving one concept by testing and modelling details
questions.explain: Development takes one promising idea and refines it through modelling, testing and detailing to improve it.

questions.q: Anthropometrics is the study of:
questions.explain: Anthropometrics is the collection and use of human body measurements to design products that fit people correctly.

questions.q: When using a percentile range in anthropometric design, choosing the 5th to 95th percentile aims to:
options: Fit only the very largest users
Fit only the average user exactly
Fit the great majority of the population
questions.explain: Designing for the 5th to 95th percentile range accommodates around 90 per cent of users, suiting most people.

questions.q: A design brief is best described as:
options: A list of every tool in the workshop
A short statement outlining the problem and what the design should achieve
questions.explain: A design brief is a concise statement that sets out the problem, the client's needs and what the design must accomplish.

questions.q: A working drawing differs from a presentation drawing because it:
options: Provides accurate dimensions and details needed to manufacture the product
Uses bright realistic colours to impress a client
questions.explain: A working drawing contains the precise dimensions, materials and details a manufacturer needs to make the product accurately.

questions.q: Evaluating a finished product against its specification helps the designer to:
options: Hide any faults from the client
Decide whether it meets the criteria and identify improvements
questions.explain: Evaluation compares the product against the specification and user needs to judge success and suggest improvements.

questions.q: A mood board is used early in the design process to:
options: Gather images, colours and textures to set a visual theme
Test the strength of a prototype
List the price of every component
questions.explain: A mood board collects visual references such as images, colours and materials to establish the look and feel of a design.

questions.q: The design process is described as 'iterative' because it:
options: Repeatedly cycles through designing, testing and improving
Follows a single fixed line from start to finish with no changes
questions.explain: An iterative design process is a repeating cycle of exploring, testing, evaluating and refining ideas to improve the product.

questions.q: The Memphis design movement of the 1980s is characterised by:
options: Bold colours, playful geometric shapes and bold patterns
questions.explain: Memphis design used bright colours, bold patterns and playful geometric forms, rejecting plain functionalism.

questions.q: A questionnaire given to potential users is an example of:
questions.explain: A questionnaire collects new first-hand data directly from users, making it a form of primary research.

questions.q: A design specification is best described as:
options: A list of measurable criteria the final product must meet
The advertising slogan for the product
A list of the designer's hobbies
questions.explain: A specification is a detailed list of criteria and requirements that the finished product must satisfy, used to guide and judge the design.

questions.q: Which type of projection shows an object's faces drawn to scale as separate front, plan and side views?
questions.explain: Orthographic projection presents an object as flat, scaled front, side and plan views, typically used for working drawings.

questions.q: Ergonomics in product design is concerned mainly with:
options: The selling price of the product
The colour of the packaging only
How comfortable, efficient and easy a product is for people to use
questions.explain: Ergonomics focuses on designing products so they are comfortable, safe and efficient for people to interact with.

questions.q: The Bauhaus design movement is best known for the principle that:
options: Form follows function, favouring simple, functional design
Only handcraft matters and machines are banned
Products should be deliberately hard to use
questions.explain: The Bauhaus promoted clean, functional design where form follows function and ornament is minimised.

questions.q: A prototype is made primarily to:
options: Sell directly to thousands of customers
Test and evaluate a design before final production
questions.explain: A prototype is a working model used to test, evaluate and refine a design before committing to full production.

questions.q: User-centred design places the greatest emphasis on:
options: The needs, wants and abilities of the people who will use the product
questions.explain: User-centred design focuses on the end users' needs and limitations throughout the design process.

questions.q: Art Deco design, popular in the 1920s and 30s, is recognised by its:
options: Bold geometric shapes, symmetry and luxurious materials
questions.explain: Art Deco features streamlined geometric forms, symmetry and rich, luxurious materials and detailing.

questions.q: An exploded diagram is used to show:
options: How parts fit together by separating them along their assembly lines
questions.explain: An exploded diagram pulls the components apart along their lines of assembly to show how they fit together.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Design & Technology (0445) syllabus; Graphic Communication
